title.narrative: Vulnerability and Adaptive Capacity of Urban Communities in a Multi-hazard coastal areas

description.narrative:
Given the high vulnerability and exposure of urban areas in Bangladesh to multiple hazards (both natural and man-made) it is important that, with partners, we improve our understanding of urban vulnerability, hazards and develop robust and sustainable resilience building methods.
Conventionally CAFOD and its partners have focused on rural community based DRR projects in addition to mainstreaming DRR thinking across other sectors such as livelihoods and humanitarian relief. However projections of urban growth and climate change indicate that urban risk will increase dramatically over the next 10 years. Resilient cities can help reduce poverty, increase growth and employment opportunities, deliver greater social equity, fresh business opportunities, more balanced ecosystems as well as better health and improved education.
In order for CAFOD and our partners to address future urban risk it is vital that we undertake a needs assessment which is interlinked with urban DRR capacity building workshop. This proposed pilot scoping study will identify and document various existing coping strategies and adaptive practices of urban households in Bangladesh. Thus this initiative will help design the next phase, a practical application to enhance adaptive capacity of some urban households.
